_meta.description: BattleScout AI dataset — BattleBots heavyweights. Builder, country, weapon and archetype are researched facts. Records carry an honest confidence label so nothing is presented as more certain than it is.

confidenceLegend.official: Win-loss from the robot's official battlebots.com profile (point-in-time, televised matches).
confidenceLegend.cited: Widely reported figure, not verified against a primary table.
confidenceLegend.est: Estimate consistent with the robot's known standing; refresh via the Bright Data pipeline for exact live numbers.
confidenceLegend.new: 2026 Pro League newcomer — no televised record yet.

_meta.koRateNote: koRate = indicative share of wins by knockout (estimated finishing tendency), not an officially published stat.
_meta.generatedBy: research-verified seed; refresh records via `npm run scrape` (Bright Data Web Unlocker)

bots.name: Orbitron
bots.note: The 2026 Pro League's headline entry — billed as the first AI-controlled combat robot, using a high-mounted camera and computer vision to drive itself. No televised record yet.

bots.name: Bite Force
bots.note: Three-time Giant Nut champion and the most successful robot of the reboot era. Retired after 2019.

bots.name: End Game
bots.note: First non-North-American televised Giant Nut champion; also won BattleBots: Champions I & II.

bots.name: Tombstone
bots.note: 2016 champion and the sport's signature hard-hitter; highest knockout tendency in the field.

bots.name: Tantrum
bots.note: Won an undefeated 2021 season; Ginger Schmidt became the first woman to captain a Giant Nut winner.

bots.name: SawBlaze
bots.note: 2022 champion; beat then-undefeated HUGE in the final. Strong control-and-damage game.

bots.name: Witch Doctor
bots.note: Perennial top-tier finisher; 2019 runner-up after winning all four season fights.

bots.name: Minotaur
bots.note: Fast, aggressive drum; 2018 runner-up and a perennial contender.

bots.name: HUGE
bots.note: Unconventional tall-wheel design that's very hard to attack; 2022 runner-up after an 8-1 season.

bots.name: Whiplash
bots.note: A control/lifter hybrid; 2020 runner-up. Wins on control and consistency more than KOs.

bots.name: Bombshell
bots.note: The 'Swiss Army Bot' with swappable weapons; 2016 runner-up.

bots.name: Hydra
bots.note: The only hydraulic flipper in BattleBots; famous multi-fight streak without being flipped.

bots.name: HyperShock
bots.note: Fast, aggressive showman; weapon configuration changes season to season.

bots.name: Riptide
bots.note: Hard-hitting 2022 rookie sensation; big KO power.

bots.name: Copperhead
bots.note: Compact, hard-hitting drum; reached the WC VII quarterfinals.

bots.name: Cobalt
bots.note: British-origin bot (Team Carbide) later run by a US team; precise energy delivery.

bots.name: Valkyrie
bots.note: Low, wedge-fronted undercutter; first female-led team to win Most Destructive.

bots.name: Black Dragon
bots.note: Long-drum spinner with excellent self-righting; strong Brazilian pedigree.

bots.name: Lock-Jaw
bots.note: Veteran team; reached the WC III semifinals.

bots.name: Skorpios
bots.weapon: Overhead spinning saw on an arm
bots.note: Aggressive overhead saw with a solid ~56% career mark.

bots.name: Rotator
bots.note: Versatile horizontal spinner; famously KO'd Tombstone ('Tombstone Killer').

bots.name: Uppercut
bots.note: Short but brutal career — 11 of 12 wins by KO, including one of the fastest ever (~25s).

bots.name: Yeti
bots.note: Fan-favorite Alaskan drum; ~65% career mark. Retired 2022.

bots.name: Bronco
bots.note: Explosive pneumatic flipper; Season 1 semifinalist and long-time fan favorite.

bots.name: Shatter!
bots.note: One of the few effective hammer bots; wins on control and points.

bots.name: Icewave
bots.note: Uniquely gas-powered horizontal spinner; veteran competitor.

bots.name: Gruff
bots.note: Armored control bot; grinds out judges' decisions.

bots.name: HiJinx
bots.note: Steel undercutter run by an Oakland team.

bots.name: Fusion
bots.note: Rare dual-weapon design with high KO potential when it connects.

bots.name: Blip
bots.note: Internal flywheel stores energy for huge flips; beat a defending champ as a rookie.

bots.name: Beta
bots.note: Legendary UK hammer bot with a devastating overhead strike.

bots.name: Deep Six
bots.note: Enormous energy but self-destructive — big hits, low reliability.

bots.name: Lucky
bots.note: Strong self-righting flipper; better in Desperado brackets than main seasons.

bots.name: Free Shipping
bots.note: Control/lifter bot; won a BattleBots: Champions II bracket.

bots.name: Captain Shrederator
bots.note: Explosive full-body shell but historically inconsistent; upset Tombstone in 2021.

bots.name: Kraken
bots.note: Rare crusher/bite weapon — a fan spectacle more than a title threat.

bots.name: Mammoth
bots.note: The largest modern heavyweight; has launched an opponent clean out of the arena.
